findings.title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in inline JavaScript
findings.body: The `request.referer` value is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal without any escaping: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. Although the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter validates the referer's host, the referer string can still contain characters like single quotes or backslashes that break out of the JS string context. An attacker who controls the Referer header (e.g., via a crafted link or redirect from the allowed host) could inject arbitrary JavaScript into the embedded iframe, which runs in the Discourse origin.

findings.title: XSS via unescaped URL interpolated into HTML
findings.body: The `url` parameter is interpolated directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"`. While the URL is validated to start with `http://` or `https://`, it can still contain HTML metacharacters (e.g., `http://example.com/'>`). Since posts are stored with `cook_method: :raw_html` and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, this allows stored XSS in the embed view.

findings.title: Weak origin validation using substring match
findings.body: The postMessage origin check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, which is a substring test rather than an exact origin comparison. If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, a malicious origin like `https://forum.example` (a different domain) would pass the check because it is a prefix of `discourseUrl`. The check should parse the URL and compare the origin exactly (protocol + host + port).

findings.title: NoMethodError when RSS item has no content element
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` when an RSS/Atom feed item does not have a `content` element (many feeds only provide `description`). This will crash the entire feed polling job, preventing all items from being imported.

findings.title: NoMethodError when embed_by_username site setting is blank
findings.body: `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` will raise `NoMethodError` if the `embed_by_username` setting is blank or nil. The `fetch_http` method is called from `perform_retrieve` without checking whether `embed_by_username` is configured, unlike `PollFeed#execute` which guards against this. This can crash the RetrieveTopic background job.

findings.title: Incorrect default port check in absolutize_urls
findings.body: The condition `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` does not account for the URL scheme. An HTTPS URL on port 80 (unusual but valid) would incorrectly get `:80` appended, and an HTTP URL on port 443 would incorrectly get `:443` appended. The check should be scheme-aware: omit the port only when it matches the default for the scheme (80 for http, 443 for https).

findings.title: Server-side request via open() without scheme validation in import_remote
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` without validating the URL scheme. While callers like `TopicEmbed.import` check for `https?://`, `import_remote` is a public method that can be called directly (e.g., from the disqus.thor task with `t[:link]`). Ruby's `open` with `open-uri` can be abused with certain inputs. A scheme validation should be added at the `import_remote` level as defense in depth.

findings.title: Unnecessary user_id passed to RetrieveTopic job for anonymous users
findings.body: When `current_user` is nil (anonymous visitor), `current_user.try(:id)` returns nil, and the job receives `user_id: nil`. Inside the job, `User.where(id: nil).first` executes a database query that returns nil, which is harmless but wasteful. More importantly, the `no_throttle` logic in TopicRetriever relies on `user.try(:staff?)` which will be nil for anonymous users, meaning the throttle always applies—this is correct behavior but the code path is unclear.
